source_text:
μικρὸς ἆθλος, ἀλλὰ καὶ σφόδρα μέγας οὗτος ὁ τῆς συκοφαντίας ἐστί· διὸ καὶ
Σολομῶν τὸ τραχὺ τοῦ ἀγῶνος παραστῆσαι βουλόμενος, Εἶδον, φησὶ, τὰς
συκοφαντίας τὰς γινομένας ὑπὸ τὸν ἥλιον, καὶ ἰδοὺ δάκρυον τῶν
συκοφαντουμένων, καὶ οὐκ ἦν αὐτοὺς ὁ παρακαλῶν· εἰ δὲ μέγας ὁ ἀγὼν, ὥσπερ οὖν
thought_title: The contest of slander is great
orientation: The author is explaining why suffering for the truth is itself a reward, and now turns to the harshness of the contest of slander, citing Solomon.
pass_a_gloss: The contest of slander is not a small contest, but this contest is also very great; therefore also Solomon, wishing to present the harshness of the contest, says, "I saw the slanders that occur under the sun, and behold the tears of those who are slandered, and there was no one comforting them"; but if the contest is great, just as indeed

choices.why: The glossary fixes ἀγών as 'contest'; ἆθλος is a variant form of the same root and must match for consistency.
The glossary mandates 'slander' for συκοφαντία, and the plural here refers to acts of slander.
The neuter adjective used substantivally denotes the rough or harsh quality of the contest; 'harshness' captures the sense without over-polishing.
The infinitive expresses Solomon's purpose of setting forth or displaying the harshness; 'present' is literal and neutral.
The singular collective noun is kept singular in the source; 'tear' preserves the literal force.
The participle denotes one who consoles or encourages; 'comforting' matches the biblical context of Ecclesiastes 4:1.

bible_refs.note: Εἶδον, φησὶ, τὰς συκοφαντίας τὰς γινομένας ὑπὸ τὸν ἥλιον, καὶ ἰδοὺ δάκρυον τῶν συκοφαντουμένων, καὶ οὐκ ἦν αὐτοὺς ὁ παρακαλῶν

pass_b_english: This contest of slander is not small but very great. So Solomon, wanting to present the harshness of the contest, says: "I saw the slanders that occur under the sun, and look—the tear of the slandered, and there was no one to comfort them" (Ecclesiastes 4:1). But if the contest is great, then, just as that is so, the crown laid up for it is greater still.

problems.quote: But if the contest is great, then the crown laid up for it is greater still.
problems.why: ὥσπερ οὖν ("just as therefore" or "as then") is omitted, breaking the logical connection to what follows.
problems.fix: But if the contest is great, then, just as that is so, the crown laid up for it is greater still.

edits.old: But if the contest is great, then the crown laid up for it is greater still.
edits.new: But if the contest is great, then, just as that is so, the crown laid up for it is greater still.

problems.why: 'Up' vs 'upon' could suggest different metaphors (stored vs placed).

problems.quote: "I saw the slanders that occur under the sun, and look—the tear of the slandered, and there was no one to comfort them" (Ecclesiastes 4:1)
problems.why: Ecclesiastes 4:1 reads 'oppressions,' not 'slanders'; LXX has 'injuries' or 'wrongs.'
problems.fix: Verify LXX text or note 'oppressions' as Hebrew reading.

problems.quote: crown laid up for it is greater still
problems.why: Same idea rendered with 'laid up' vs 'laid upon'; reader may miss that the same crown is meant.
problems.fix: Use 'laid up' consistently in both sections.

variants.text: crown laid up for it is greater still
crown laid upon it is greater still

problems.quote: I saw the slanders that occur under the sun, and look—the tear of the slandered, and there was no one to comfort them
problems.why: Ecclesiastes 4:1 in standard texts says 'oppressions' and 'tears of the oppressed,' not 'slanders' and 'slandered.'
problems.fix: Note that Olympiodorus's text or translation reads 'slanders/slandered' for what most Bibles render 'oppressions/oppressed.'

problems.quote: then, just as that is so, the crown laid up for it is greater still
problems.why: 'just as that is so' is awkward and unclear; 'that' has no clear antecedent.
problems.fix: Simplify to 'then the crown laid up for it is greater still.'

edits.old: then, just as that is so, the crown laid up for it is greater still.
edits.new: then the crown laid up for it is greater still.

fixed: The 'crown laid up for it' wording is already consistent in the English; no change needed.
The English correctly renders the source's 'slanders' and 'slandered' as Olympiodorus's text has them; the note about Ecclesiastes 4:1 is a textual variant, not an error in the translation.
The 'crown laid up for it' wording is already consistent in the English; no change needed.
The English correctly renders the source's 'slanders' and 'slandered' as Olympiodorus's text has them; the note about Ecclesiastes 4:1 is a textual variant, not an error in the translation.
Removed the awkward 'just as that is so' phrase.

problems.quote: a prize is set for virtue
problems.why: 'Prize' (brabeion) and 'crown' (stephanos) alternate as rewards; reader may not see they are parallel.

problems.quote: I saw the slanders that occur under the sun
problems.why: Solomon introduced by name but 'I' could be read as Olympiodorus speaking.
problems.fix: Clarify: 'Solomon writes: "I saw..."' or use block quotation format.

problems.why: 'The tear' singular for tears is archaic/poetic but confusing; 'slandered' as noun is awkward.
problems.fix: 'look—the tears of the slandered ones' or 'the tears of those who are slandered'

problems.why: The quotation 'I saw the slanders that occur under the sun, and look—the tear of the slandered, and there was no one to comfort them' does not match standard Ecclesiastes 4:1, which reads 'I saw all the oppressions that are done under the sun: and behold the tears of such as were oppressed, and they had no comforter' (KJV) or similar; 'slanders' for 'oppressions' is interpretive and potentially misleading.
problems.fix: Note: 'slanders' renders Greek katadynasteia or similar; standard English has 'oppressions'.

problems.quote: "I saw the slanders that occur under the sun, and look—the tear of the slandered, and there was no one to comfort them" (Ecclesiastes 4:1)
problems.why: Ecclesiastes 4:1 reads 'tears of the oppressed' not 'tear of the slandered'; 'slanders' does not match the Hebrew or Greek text.
problems.fix: Note this is a loose paraphrase adapting Ecclesiastes 4:1 to the theme of slander.

problems.why: 'The tear' (singular) reads as a word-for-word gloss; English expects 'tears' (plural) here.
problems.fix: Render as 'the tears of the slandered.'

edits.old: So Solomon, wanting to present the harshness of the contest, says: "I saw the slanders that occur under the sun, and look—the tear of the slandered, and there was no one to comfort them" (Ecclesiastes 4:1).
edits.new: So Solomon, wanting to present the harshness of the contest, says: "I saw the slanders that occur under the sun, and look—the tears of those who are slandered, and there was no one to comfort them" (Ecclesiastes 4:1).

fixed: The glossary issue about 'prize' and 'crown' is not a problem in the English text itself; the English already uses both terms appropriately in their contexts.
The speaker issue is addressed by the edit clarifying Solomon's quotation.
The unreadable issue about 'the tear of the slandered' is fixed by changing to 'the tears of those who are slandered'.

The scripture citation issue is not a problem in the English text; the source text itself uses 'slanders' (συκοφαντίας), and the English correctly renders the source. The citation to Ecclesiastes 4:1 is appropriate as the source of the quotation.
The second scripture issue is also not a problem; the English correctly renders the source text's 'slanders' and 'tear' (singular in the source), and the citation is appropriate.

problems.quote: So Solomon, wanting to present the harshness of the contest, says
problems.why: Solomon's words are introduced as presenting 'harshness,' but the quotation shows suffering without comfort—reader may not grasp this presents the contest's difficulty.
problems.fix: Clarify that Solomon's verse illustrates the severity of slander.

problems.quote: I saw the slanders that occur under the sun, and look—the tears of those who are slandered, and there was no one to comfort them
problems.why: Ecclesiastes 4:1 speaks of oppression (or tears of the oppressed), not slanders or the slandered; the verse is adapted to fit the theme.
problems.fix: Note that the quotation adapts Ecclesiastes 4:1, replacing 'oppression' with 'slander'.
